prompt: Build a thread-safe counter with a synchronized increment method, then hammer it from many threads at once and prove no increments are lost. Complete the SyncCounter class.
explanation: count++ is secretly three steps (read, add, write), so two unsynchronized threads can read the same value and lose an increment. Marking increment() synchronized makes each call hold the object's monitor lock, so the three steps run atomically and hammer returns exactly threads * perThread. Reading value() after join() is safe without synchronization because join() guarantees all the workers' writes are visible to the joining thread.
hints: Store the count in a private int field; increment() just does count++, and the synchronized keyword on the method supplies the locking.
In hammer, create one SyncCounter, then fill a Thread[] where each thread's lambda loops perThread times calling counter.increment().
Start every thread first, then join every thread in a second loop, and only then return counter.value().
